findings.summary: StaticStreamWorkbench.call_tool_stream does not resolve override names back to original tool names, unlike call_tool which correctly uses _override_name_to_original
findings.failure_scenario: User creates StaticStreamWorkbench(tools=[tool_named_double], tool_overrides={'double': ToolOverride(name='multiply_by_two')}). AssistantAgent checks isinstance(wb, StaticStreamWorkbench) and routes to call_tool_stream('multiply_by_two', ...). Line 185 does tool.name == name against the original tools list (which only has 'double'), so the tool is not found and an error result is returned instead of executing the tool.

findings.summary: McpWorkbench.list_tools does not detect when an override renames a tool to a name that conflicts with another tool from the MCP server, producing duplicate names and silently unreachable tools
findings.failure_scenario: MCP server provides tools 'fetch' and 'search'. User passes tool_overrides={'fetch': ToolOverride(name='search')}. list_tools returns two ToolSchemas both named 'search'. call_tool('search', ...) resolves via _override_name_to_original to 'fetch', so the real 'search' tool is unreachable by its name. StaticWorkbench catches this at construction via existing_tool_names check, but McpWorkbench has no equivalent validation.
